description: Canonical schema for the replay CSV consumed by the on-device engine's replay harness (S-06) and produced by any synthetic-data generator or IO-VNBD conversion script on the ML side. This file is the ground truth for column names, order, dtype and units. sample_replay.csv is a literal, valid example. validate_replay_csv.py enforces this schema and must pass before a CSV is handed across tracks.

columns.name: timestamp_ms
columns.notes: strictly increasing within a sequence; no two rows share a timestamp

columns.name: accel_x
columns.notes: vehicle-frame-aligned if alignment has run, else raw phone-frame

columns.name: gnss_valid
columns.notes: 1 iff this row carries a real GNSS fix; when 0 the four gnss_* fields below MUST be empty, not 0.0 — zero is a valid latitude and must never be used as a missing-value sentinel

missing_value_representation: empty string between commas, e.g. `,,` — never 0, never NaN, never the string "null" or "NA"
known_failure_modes_this_schema_prevents: Excel re-saving a CSV on a device with a non-US regional format silently swaps the decimal separator to a comma, which is a delimiter collision with a comma-delimited file. Never open/re-save these files in Excel; edit with a script or a plain text editor only.

Windows text editors defaulting to CRLF line endings, which some CSV parsers (including naive Kotlin BufferedReader splits) will include as a trailing \r in the last field of every row. .gitattributes forces LF on checkout; validate_replay_csv.py checks for stray \r bytes.

gyro in deg/s instead of rad/s is the single most common unit bug in this whole project (factor of ~57x) and produces a filter that silently diverges rather than crashing. Every producer of this file must assert on gyro magnitude sanity (see contracts/units.md).
Using 0.0 instead of an empty field for a missing GNSS fix — 0,0 is a valid coordinate (off the coast of West Africa) and will silently corrupt map matching instead of erroring.
